# Rally

## Mental model

Rally is a Gleam package for building Lustre apps that render on the server and hydrate in the browser. You write page modules with page-local models, messages, load handlers, save handlers, views, and broadcast hooks. Rally generates routing composition, server-side rendering, WebSocket transport, request/result protocol code, hydration, browser lifecycle, and typed client-server messaging.

The page file is the contract. Client state, server calls, and the message types that cross the wire live together until you extract shared code.

Rally is opinionated and convention-driven. Rally apps use SQLite for the application database, Marmot for SQL migrations and type-safe query generation, Proute for file-based routing and page dispatch, Libero for typed wire codecs, and Lustre for browser-side TEA. If an app needs a different foundation such as PostgreSQL, fork Rally and submit a tested PR instead of adding local framework glue.

ETF is the default wire format. JSON is available for non-Gleam clients.

## Quick start

```sh
gleam new my_app
cd my_app
gleam add rally libero
gleam run -m rally init
gleam run -m rally build
gleam run
```

`rally init` creates the Rally Scoreboard Example starter app. `rally gen` runs configured Marmot codegen, runs Proute when `proute.toml` exists, and generates Rally/Libero glue under `src/generated/**`. `rally regen` deletes `src/generated` first, then runs `gen`. `rally build` runs `gen` and builds the current package for Erlang and JavaScript. `rally migrate` delegates to Marmot migrate, and `rally reset` delegates to Marmot reset. Rally has no migration runner of its own. `rally server` stops any process listening on `PORT` or 8080, then runs `gleam run` in the foreground. Open `http://localhost:8080` to see the app. To use a different port, set `PORT` in `.env` or run `PORT=8081 gleam run -m rally server`.

Rally checks delegated package dependencies before shelling out. `[tools.marmot]` requires a direct `marmot` dependency, `proute.toml` requires `proute`, and Rally/Libero wire codegen requires `libero`.

`APP_ENV=dev` is the default. Set `APP_ENV=prod` in production for secure session cookies and quieter console output.

## Generator surfaces

`rally build` is the Rally Scoreboard Example generator path. Authored pages own `Model`, `Message`, `ServerMsg`, `initial_model`, optional `init`, `load`, optional `handle`, `broadcast_subscriptions`, and `apply_broadcast`. Proute owns route params, query params, page enums, and page dispatch. Rally owns transport, request/result encoding, hydration, SSR composition, browser boot, topic sync, server-side broadcast filtering, and generated browser lifecycle glue.

## Page conventions

A page file in `src/<namespace>/pages/` maps to a URL route. The filename determines the route:

| File | URL | Route variant |
|---|---|---|
| `home_.gleam` | `/` | `Home` |
| `about.gleam` | `/about` | `About` |
| `games.gleam` | `/games` | `Games` |
| `products/id_.gleam` | `/products/:id` | `ProductsId(id: Int)` |

`home_.gleam` is the default route for the directory it lives in. Trailing underscore marks a dynamic segment. Names ending in `_id` become `Int` params; everything else `String`.

### Required exports

```gleam
pub type Model { ... }
pub type Message { ... }
pub fn initial_model(page_shared_state, query_params) -> Model
pub fn update(model: Model, msg: Message) -> #(Model, Effect(Message))
pub fn view(model: Model) -> Element(Message)
```

Dynamic routes receive generated route params in `initial_model`, optional `init`, and route-aware hooks. Page shared state is app-defined per mount and constructed by generated Proute glue.

### SSR loading

Pages can export Erlang-targeted `load` for server-side data fetch before first render. Rally encodes load results through generated Libero codecs, embeds hydration flags in the document, and reuses the same result type for browser navigation loads.

### Layouts

`app_shell.gleam` provides standard page chrome for the generated browser mount and SSR document composition. Proute page modules own page dispatch; Rally owns browser lifecycle and hydration.

## Server messaging

### Load and save handlers

Page-local `ServerMsg`, `LoadResult`, `load`, and optional `handle` exports are the Rally Scoreboard surface:

```gleam
pub type ServerMsg { PublicHomeLoad; PublicHomeIncrement }
pub type LoadResult { PublicHomeLoaded(count: Int) }
pub fn load(db: sqlight.Connection) -> Result(Int, load.LoadError)
pub fn handle(db: sqlight.Connection, message: ServerMsg) -> Result(Update, SaveError)
```

Generated browser modules expose page-specific save functions such as `generated/rally/server.save_public_home`. Generated SSR and browser lifecycle glue call `load` through the same typed wire contract. Rally treats page handler signatures as the source of truth, turns their wire-visible types into Libero seeds, and uses the generated Libero codecs from Rally-owned protocol glue.

### Broadcast

Broadcast-aware pages define typed topics and event payloads in app code, usually in a shared `broadcasts.gleam` module. Page `broadcast_subscriptions` hooks express interest for the current model or route, and page `apply_broadcast` hooks merge decoded events into the page model. Keep both hooks together in a `// BROADCAST` section.

Rally maps typed topics to compact text topic frames, stores active subscriptions per connection, filters broadcasts on the server, and does not send a broadcast back to the initiating connection.

## Runtime modules

Most Rally apps import only a few `rally/runtime/*` modules:

| Module | Use it for |
|---|---|
| `rally/runtime/load` | Standard page load error type |
| `rally/runtime/db` | SQLite open, timed queries, nested transactions, SQL value helpers |
| `rally/runtime/system` | App startup and background jobs |
| `rally/runtime/session` | Session cookie generation, parsing, response headers |
| `rally/runtime/auth` | Auth policy and load result types |
| `rally/runtime/env` | `APP_ENV` parsing, production cookie policy |
| `rally/runtime/test_db` | Fast in-memory SQLite for tests |

Generated code also imports internal runtime modules for wire encoding, SSR,
topic fan-out, background jobs, and WebSocket process state. App code should
treat those as private and import the modules above instead.

## Configuration

```toml
[tools.rally.context]
module = "sqlight"
type = "Connection"

[tools.marmot]
database = "db/dev.sqlite"
sql_dir = "src/sql"
output = "src/generated/sql"

[proute]
pages_root = "src"

[[proute.mounts]]
name = "public"
route_root = "/"
```

Rally reads standard project config from `gleam.toml` and `proute.toml`. `rally build` runs Marmot when `[tools.marmot]` is present, runs Proute when `proute.toml` exists, then generates Rally and Libero files under `src/generated/**`.

### Context types

**Load context** (`[tools.rally.context]`): server-side value passed to page `load` and `handle` functions. The starter app uses `sqlight.Connection`.

**Page shared state** (`src/<mount>/page_shared_state.gleam`): app-defined state visible to page initializers in a mount. Use it for page-visible shared values, not shell-only browser state.

**Shell state**: browser-only state owned by the generated mount config and `app_shell.gleam`, such as active path and dark mode.

## Generated files

Running `gleam run -m rally build` produces:

Generated files stay in the app package:

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `src/generated/proute/**` | Route types, route params, query params, and page dispatch |
| `src/generated/rally/**` | Request/result protocols, client transport, browser mount/app glue, hydration, SSR, WS, theme, load/save result envelopes |
| `src/generated/libero/**` | ETF codec helpers, decoder registration, atoms/wire modules, and Libero contract metadata |

## Internals

The `rally/internal/...` modules are Rally's codegen implementation. App code should treat them as private.

### Pipeline

```text
gleam.toml + proute.toml -> Marmot -> Proute -> Rally load/save discovery -> Libero codec graph -> generated Rally glue -> Erlang and JavaScript builds
```

### Codegen modules (`src/rally/internal/`)

| Module | Role |
|---|---|
| `rally.gleam` | CLI entry point and Rally Scoreboard Example build orchestration |
| `internal/init.gleam` | Rally starter scaffold generation |
| `internal/generator/load_rpc.gleam` | Rally Scoreboard Example load/save, SSR, browser, hydration, WebSocket, topic, and protocol generation |
| `internal/format.gleam` | Runs `gleam format` on generated code |

Libero provides seed-driven type graph walking, codegen_decoders, field_type, glance_type_resolver (shared Glance type resolution), wire_identity (canonical type hashing), ETF codec generation, JSON codec generation, decoder registration, atom registration, wire modules, and contract metadata. Rally discovers page-local load/save/broadcast contracts first, feeds the reachable wire types into Libero, then generates Rally-owned request/result, transport, dispatch, hydration, SSR, and browser lifecycle glue around those codecs.

### Auth framework

`rally/runtime/auth` contains shared auth types and helpers for password hashing, short login codes, provider sessions, and page load auth results. `rally/runtime/auth_http` owns the standard email-code and Google provider HTTP route mechanics. Apps provide callbacks for user lookup/upsert, code storage/delivery, OAuth credentials, provider identity verification, return-path narrowing, and authorization policy.

### Transport

WebSocket with auto-reconnect for browser load/save requests and broadcasts. SSR renders full HTML with embedded flags on first request; the client reads flags and boots as a SPA.

### Dev tools

Message inspector enabled in `APP_ENV=dev`. Browser console shows `->` (client to server, orange), `<-` (server response, blue), `<<` (server-to-client frame, purple). Responses include round-trip latency. `window.__RALLY_MESSAGES__` holds the full message history.

## Verification

```sh
gleam test
gleam format --check
gleam docs build
```

Integration check with the curling/v3 app:

```sh
cd /Users/daverapin/projects/curling/v3
bin/regen
gleam run -m rally build
gleam run
```
